transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 16:00 UTC (scheduled 30/45 mins, ran 48)
Duration reported: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Alex Torres (Redwood CSM), Lena Park (CrossMotion Head of Cloud Partnerships), Marcus Reed (VP Growth), Sara Iqbal (Solutions Architect), Tom Hale (Legal Ops)

Summary (auto): quick partner alignment and deal triage; discuss co-sell mechanics, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), initial volume & latency expectations, potential legal/redline items; agree next steps for pricing and a short pilot.

Topics (auto): co-sell GTM cadence; trial / Dedicated capacity quote; latency/cost tradeoffs; data residency and legal touchpoints; competitive positioning

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jordan from Redwood, I'll kick off, with Priya and Alex from our team. Lena, Marcus, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Lena Park: yeah thanks Jordan. quick agenda from our side is, uh, make sure we've got the right commercial levers, understand the technical constraints for a pilot, and then sort who owns what on the co-sell side.
[00:22] Marcus Reed: and also, we need to check how this sits with our incumbent partners, so, you know, call out overlaps with, uh, VeloxAI or Nimbus if we see them.
[00:31] Priya Singh: cool. technically we want to cover expected qps and latency SLOs, model mix, and what environment you'd prefer — hosted redwood api, dedicated reserved pool, or private vpc/on-prem.
[00:42] Sara Iqbal: quick note — our legal/infosec will want KMS and audit logs for any prod pilot, so plato. I mean — so please include encryption details.
[00:52] Tom Hale: yeah from legal i'll just be looking at data flow and retention, ok.
[00:55] Jordan Kim: perfect, we'll put those in the follow-up pack. to start: whats the primary use case? Lena?
[01:03] Lena Park: CrossMotion is building a personalized in-app assistant across our SaaS product — light generative content and routing to product pages, so prompt patterns are short but with moderate context. expected initial pilot is 2k concurrent sessions at peak, roughly 1–2 requests per session per minute.
[01:20] Priya Singh: that helps. model-wise, are you leaning open models or license — like open-reach or vendor models?
[01:26] Marcus Reed: we prefer open models for cost and auditability, but we might want a higher-quality backbone for some flows. and importantly, we need predictable cost so dedicated capacity is appealing.
[01:38] Priya Singh: noted. for 2k concurrent sessions we typically suggest a Dedicated pool or hybrid: host the lower-critical flows on hosted to save ops, and pin high-priority flows to Dedicated. that gives you predictable tail latency.
[01:52] Lena Park: tbvh — what's the delta in unit cost between hosted and dedicated? ballpark is fine.
[01:57] Jordan Kim: ballpark: hosted per-token you pay utility pricing; Dedicated moves you to committed monthly commit with significantly lower per-token and predictable throughput. I'll send a table — but rough, you can see 30–50% per-token savings depending on utilization and quantization.
[02:13] Marcus Reed: 30–50% is meaningful. what about cold-start latency and kv cache, if users resume sessions?
[02:20] Priya Singh: Dedicated lets you keep warmed KV cache and stash prefixes so resumed sessions are sub-100ms on average for short prompts; hosted can do caching but less control. caveat: exact numbers depend on prompt size and model.
[02:34] Sara Iqbal: can you say more about compatibility with on-prem connectors? we have some regulated customers where PII never leaves their region.
[02:42] Priya Singh: yes — our Private offering can run in a VPC or on-prem with a private control plane; you'll get KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs surfaced to your SIEM. there are extra ops steps and a longer lead time for air-gapped installs.
[02:54] Lena Park: how long is the lead time?
[02:56] Priya Singh: typical private deploy lead time is 8–12 weeks depending on infra readiness; Dedicated is faster — often a week or two to provision a reserved pool.
[03:07] Marcus Reed: legal question: is there a template SOW and liability language we should review?
[03:12] Alex Torres: yes, I can share our Dedicated SOW template and standard SLAs. I noted Tom on the call, we can start with the template and highlight partner-specific clauses.
[03:20] Tom Hale: thanks. also need clarity on data retention defaults and the option to purge logs on customer request.
[03:28] Jordan Kim: we'll include data retention options in the follow-up.
[03:31] [small cross talk]
[03:35] Marcus Reed: question on fallback: if Dedicated is saturated, is there an automated fallback to hosted models?
[03:41] Priya Singh: yes, smart routing can failover by policy to hosted or other model variants. you define fallback rules and can set cost vs latency priorities. note sometimes model outputs differ slightly so we generally recommend canarying.
[03:55] Lena Park: ok can we get an example of the canary plan? what does a canary rollout look like?
[04:02] Priya Singh: typical canary: route a small percentage (5–10%) to the new model variant, monitor quality/regressions on a prompt set, then increase if good. our Console shows per-route metrics.
[04:14] Lena Park: will you include a short demo of the Console metrics in the follow-up?
[04:18] Jordan Kim: yes, i'll drop a recorded gif and screenshots.
[04:21] Marcus Reed: who owns the GTM from Redwood side for co-sell?
[04:25] Jordan Kim: me for the AE motion and Alex for post-sale/CSM. we'll coordinate with your GTM owners.
[04:31] Lena Park: ok. competitive — Marcus mentioned VeloxAI; how do you differentiate in pricing and reliability?
[04:38] Jordan Kim: big differentiator is unified runtime and batching optimizations that give predictable latency at scale; we also focus on dev ergonomics and observability for partner-led deals. pricing we can be aggressive on co-sell terms.
[04:49] Marcus Reed: good. any known limitations on model bed sizes or sequence lengths we should plan for?
[04:55] Priya Singh: models with very long context have different memory and kernel profiles; we have quantization and kernel selection to handle most, but super long 64k+ sequences need specific planning. for your initial prompt families it sounds fine.
[05:07] [silence / note typing]
[05:10] Sara Iqbal: quick technical: can we run a short perf bench — 10 minute run — to validate latency on our sample prompts before the pilot?
[05:17] Priya Singh: absolutely — if you share the prompt set and a traffic pattern csv we'll run a scoped perf test on a Dedicated config and share results.
[05:24] Lena Park: we'll send that. next, co-sell economics — how do you typically split ACV and lead credit?
[05:31] Jordan Kim: we do flexible partner economics depending on motion — referral vs joint Exec-led co-sell. for an initial pilot we can agree to a waived setup and backloaded revenue share once we reach committed spend. we'll propose specifics in the partner packet.
[05:44] Marcus Reed: ok. legal: are you ok with mutual indemnities typical for enterprise SaaS?
[05:49] Tom Hale: uh, mutual indemnities plus data handling clauses; we'll redline.
[05:53] Alex Torres: noted. I'll attach the SOW and standard security packet.
[05:57] Jordan Kim: quick risk triage — items we flag: 1) data residency for regulated accounts, 2) pilot size and measurement plan, 3) fallback behavior and quality regressions, 4) commercial terms and lead credit. any more?
[06:12] Lena Park: partner enablement cadence — we need a 90-day enablement plan for sales and then a co-marketing one-pager.
[06:19] Jordan Kim: we can provide a 90-day enablement checklist and a co-marketing asset template.
[06:24] Marcus Reed: one more, can we get a cost sensitivity table for different utilization ranges? 50%, 75%, 90% — that helps our finance team.
[06:33] Priya Singh: yes we can run utilization scenarios and show per-token line items with Dedicated and hosted comparatives.
[06:39] Lena Park: timeline — we'd like to have internal decision by first week of Jan so we can start a Q1 pilot.
[06:45] Jordan Kim: sounds good.
[06:47] Marcus Reed: sidenote — if there are special compliance requirements for some EU customers, how does Redwood handle data residency?
[06:54] Priya Singh: we have regioned endpoints and Private deployments; for EU-only tenancy we can do a VPC private control plane in a specified region, but that may affect lead times and costs.
[07:06] Lena Park: ok, final quick thing — could you include a short note on potential competitive mitigation vs InferaCloud? specifically, where Redwood can show faster tail latencies.
[07:15] Jordan Kim: yes i'll include benchmarking notes and where our batching and runtime optimizations show improvements.
[07:21] [wrap-up]
[07:23] Jordan Kim: alright, recap quickly: Jordan to send partner packet (one-pager, pricing tiers, co-sell terms), Priya to run latency/cost scenarios and perf bench after CrossMotion shares prompts and traffic, Alex to share SOW and security docs, Lena to confirm GTM owners and internal decision timeline. we'll sync next week if needed and aim for exec briefing the week of 2026-12-27.
[07:41] Lena Park: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[07:44] Tom Hale: thanks.
[07:45] Jordan Kim: thanks, we'll follow up in email with the attachments.
